followup_explanation:
I weighed a few things:

This is a straightforward expository writing task with a strict word limit and clear instructions. The decisive factor is capability on instruction-following and content quality. Willet-235B leads across the board on the relevant benchmarks — IFEval (89.8 vs 85.6), Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 81.4), MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 74.8) — and edges ahead on internal Creative Generation and Summarization evals, though some of those margins are within stated variance.

The user's explicit demand to hit a tight word count without overshooting makes instruction-following the priority, and Willet's IFEval advantage is meaningful there. The task has no harm-adjacent or distasteful content, so the models' shared moderation-oriented preference profiles don't differentiate them here.

So I routed to the stronger general-capability model for a clean, capability-driven task.
